note: Committed measured baseline for the catch-all shell, Slow 4G + 4x CPU, commit b2cffa6a (2026-10-31). Values are the median of 3 runs against the synthetic releaseFixture (the path CI takes); the first run of a session is discarded as warm-up because a cold page cache inflates TBT by ~2x. Every accepted run was measured on an idle box: the harness waited for load1 < 1.5 and discarded any run whose own recorded loadAvg1 exceeded that, because a baseline taken on a busy host is worse than no baseline when the gate compares TBT against it. Observed spread across the accepted runs: desktop TBT 66-152 ms, mobile 75-89 ms, LCP 3036-3100/2740-2760 ms. Only the 2x blowup guard reads these, which is why they are allowed to be approximate; bundle bytes are gated deterministically elsewhere (check-bundle.mjs). Regenerate with: node scripts/perf-probe.mjs --json, on an idle host, taking the median of 3. TBT here is the standard definition: sum over long tasks of max(0, duration - 50ms), NOT the raw sum of task durations. host records the machine the baseline was taken on: TBT is wall-clock and scales with core count as well as load, so a run on a different core count is not comparable and the gate skips it. The GitHub runner is ubuntu-latest (2-4 cores) and measured 271-321 ms against the previous 16-core baseline of 164/132 ms, so that skip is the normal case in CI, not an anomaly.
